look_here_first: EXAMINE FOUR THINGS IN THIS ORDER: (1) alternate simple leaves 4–7 cm, often 1–4 LOBES on each side and strong teeth; (2) woolly/white-hairy NEW twigs and flower cups; (3) 20 stamens whose ANTHERS are ROSE–PURPLE (not cream) in open white flower; (4) red pome 9–14 mm usually, 4–5 hard stones. Thorns may be present or absent, so never key this species on a thorn alone.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Deciduous shrub/small tree, up to about 10 m in FNA broad description, often shorter. Rough fissured gray-brown bark and woody determinate thorns may occur.

key_traits.label: Twigs thorns
key_traits.text: Newest twig growth woolly (lanate) and older pale gray to tan. Straight woody twigs thorns absent to frequent, often 4–5 cm on two-year-old stems; may turn chestnut brown or black.

key_traits.label: Leaf arrangement
key_traits.text: Alternate SIMPLE leaves on woody shoots, not opposite; 4–7 cm broad elliptic to rhombic-ovate, basal margin less toothed, distal margin strongly serrate; 1–4 lobes per side. Tip and lobe depth variable, hairier underside when young.

key_traits.label: Leaf variety warning
key_traits.text: FNA var. texana typically 2–4 deep lobes per side; var. dasyphylla more often 1–2(–3) shallow lobes. Do not claim exact variety from one leaf photograph.

key_traits.label: Flower clusters
key_traits.text: Usually 7–12 flowers per broad, somewhat flat cluster; white 5-petaled flowers ~14–22 mm across, flower cup/hypanthium downy-hairy.

key_traits.label: Stamens anthers
key_traits.text: About 20 stamens; anthers rose/rose-purple, red or purple. The colored anther is a KEY character in contrast to ivory/cream on C. mollis and usually C. viridis. Confirm before anthers shed pollen or darken/dry.

key_traits.label: Styles
key_traits.text: 4 or 5 styles, often delicate at flower center. Requires macro; not reliably countable in general flower photo.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Red or orange-red miniature apple-like pome, usually 9–14 mm diameter, sometimes to 25 mm, with 4–5 hard inner pyrenes. Fruit COLOR alone not diagnostic.

key_traits.label: Habitat
key_traits.text: Rich bottomlands or river bottoms, alluvial rich soils and open woodland/brush margins; often near water and in southeastern/central Texas broad regional references. Do not infer local Hays nativity from habitat.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: 4–7 cm lobed and strongly toothed alternate leaves

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: woolly new twigs / downy flower cups

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: woody lateral thorns often 4–5 cm but variably absent
